I'll start by reading the orchestration skill and gathering the run metadata in parallel.
Evidence is conclusive. Writing the reports.

**The bottleneck is upstream provider latency on the Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` path. Nothing local is slow.**

## Measured

Two events, both inside single provider requests.

**03:40:59–03:49:28Z — five `ws_close_1011` upstream failures**, one per Luna audit run, after 523–1654 s hangs each. Close code 1011 is an upstream internal error.

**03:50:16–04:33:17Z — the 39-minute stall.** Each run reissued its turn. Every reissue held for ~2300 s and released in near-FIFO submission order:

| run | id | issued | released | wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| catalog | 31a5591b | 03:50:16 | 04:29:41 | **2363.6 s** |
| authority | 347552a4 | 03:52:28 | 04:32:06 | **2376.5 s** |
| autopilot | 6e0672ae | 03:53:40 | 04:31:13 | **2251.2 s** |
| orchestration | b380834f | 03:54:32 | 04:33:17 | **2325.7 s** |
| reconciliation-check | 0c40ac42 | 04:13:05 | still open | **>26 min in flight** |
| runtime | ddac0df9 | — | — | no turn since 04:17:03 |

All were carrying 231k–247k input tokens.

## Every other stage measured clean

Requests are issued 0.0–1.2 s after the prior response lands, so no tool held time. `authority.md` hit disk at 04:32:00Z, six seconds before its exchange persisted at 04:32:06Z, which proves tool dispatch, execution and transcript persistence are not the bottleneck. Roster `last_turn_at` tracks `wire_exchange.ts` within seconds across all eleven panes, so there is no projection lag. The gateway served per-run health at ~1 s cadence, all HTTP 200, continuously through the stall. The proxy logged nothing since 09-02.

The `stalled` label on `ddac0df9` and `0c40ac42` is derived from `last_turn_at` age. It is the symptom.

## Controls

The **Opus portfolio** (287fcdb2) escaped by finishing at 03:47:35Z, before the stall window opened, on a different harness and provider path. It averaged 22.0 s per exchange with one 509 s tail outlier at the incident onset.

The decisive control is the **Sol investigator** (b81621b8), launched 04:29Z on the same host, proxy and gateway: 6.6–137.6 s per turn on 7k–76k context, healthy right through the stall. Same local infrastructure, low context, no problem.

## Cause

Provider capacity or queueing, aggravated by seven concurrent Luna runs on one account each re-submitting ~240k tokens per turn, roughly 1.6M tokens of aggregate prefill per fleet round. The uniform FIFO release is a draining queue, not per-request timeouts. Corroborating: my own Claude request returned `rate_limit_error` at 04:37:17Z, so account-level pressure is live now. Latency also rose with context before the incident (0c40ac42: 26.8 s at 19k, 56.8 s at 198k, and 88.4 s at 98k *after* 04:00Z versus 11.1 s at 105k before).

## Recommendation: wait. Do not restart anything.

The four runs released at 04:29–04:33Z and immediately opened new requests. They are working. Restarting discards up to 60 minutes of context and forces a fresh 240k-token prefill against the congested endpoint, which is the one action guaranteed to make this worse.

1. Hold 15 minutes, re-read roster for `31a5591b`, `347552a4`, `6e0672ae`, `b380834f`.
2. Launch no further `gpt-5.6-luna` runs until the fleet drains.
3. Watch `0c40ac42` (open since 04:13:05, should release next) and `ddac0df9` (no turn since 04:17:03).
4. Only if `ddac0df9-ab44-4277-8ea4-bed514a51dda` is still frozen after the hold, `nudge` it to write partial findings. No interrupt, no restart.

Boundaries: provider queue state is inferred from client-side timing and close codes; no provider telemetry was available. The rate-limit observation corroborates but does not prove a shared limiter across the two paths.

Run just moved — and it moved into a **third attempt of the same turn**. That changes the answer.
Stuart's CPU evidence changes the picture. Collecting attribution now.

**ddac0df9 is in a retry loop, not a slow request. And Stuart is right that I overstated "nothing local is slow" — though the CPU is not the audit's fault.**

## The run: three attempts, same payload, zero output

| attempt | issued | closed | wall | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| turn 66 | 03:49:28 | 04:17:02 | 1653.8 s | `ws_close_1011`, 0 in / 0 out |
| turn 67 #1 | 04:17:03 | 04:46:17 | 1754.2 s | closed, **no stop_reason, no tokens** |
| turn 67 #2 | 04:46:18 | in flight | — | byte-identical replay |

Both turn 67 attempts carry `request_raw_bytes = 821410` — identical. Last real output was turn 65 at 03:49:20Z. **57 minutes with no model output.** The request is 41x the last successful one (20,035 bytes): it's the full ~240k-token conversation replayed after the 1011.

Not a queue wait. Peers released with real completions (`347552a4` returned 4,086 output tokens), 30 codex exchanges completed since 04:33Z, `consolidation.json` landed at 04:41:10Z. This run alone loops.

## Effort: footer is accurate, the receipt is wrong

`request_extras.reasoning.effort` = `xhigh` on 70 of 71 exchanges from 03:28:54Z onward. The launch receipt in `runs.json` says `high`. **The footer matches the wire; the divergence is receipt-vs-wire.** Contributing, not proximate: xhigh was already in effect during the run's healthy 8-12 s turns, but it inflated tokens per turn and is consistent with this run hitting the fleet's highest context (247,078) and turn count (279).

## No runtime.md or runtime.json exists

Nothing on disk. All research is transcript-only. The 3,635-token burst at 03:48:04Z was likely the report drafted in-message. Recoverable while the pane lives.

## CPU: saturated, but ~5.3 cores are not the audit

Load average **51.44 / 147.11 / 330.48** on 12 cores. The 15-minute figure is 27x core count, peaking inside the stall window and draining.

| pid | %CPU | elapsed | process | audit? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64139 | **549.8** | **9d 02h** | Apple Virtualization VM (Docker) | **no** |
| 48471 | **84.5** | **2d 10h** | pyenv python3 | **no** |
| 9 pids, ppid 94154 | ~398 total | ~1h19m | TM capture layer | yes |

**No leaked test workers: pytest 0, vitest 0, jest 0.** The audit was read-only issue review and never ran a suite. codex binaries are 0.4-0.7% each with no orphans. The 2,600 processes / 22,185 threads are the VM, Electron helpers under `node_modules`, and desktop load.

I'm revising the earlier claim: local starvation is plausibly a co-factor on the response streaming and persistence path, and I cannot cleanly separate it from an upstream stall. What survives is the run-specific discriminator — Sol and the orchestrator took normal turns on this same saturated host while only ddac0df9 loops. Oversized payload and no CPU headroom compound.

## Recommendation

**Step 0, touches no agent:** reclaim the ~5.3 cores held by pid 64139 (VM, 9 days old) and pid 48471 (pyenv python, 2 days old). Attribution only — I signalled nothing. This may let the in-flight retry finish untouched.

**If declined or ineffective within one ~29-min cycle:** interrupt `ddac0df9-ab44-4277-8ea4-bed514a51dda`, then immediately nudge it to write `runtime.md`/`runtime.json` in one pass for issues 603, 565, 504, 482, 472, 471, 459, 460, marking unfinished ones `status: incomplete`, before any further reading. Interrupt preserves the transcript. Do not close the pane, do not launch a replacement.

**Evidence:** `wire_exchange` in `transport_matters_preview` filtered to that run_id; `runs.json`; project directory listing; `uptime` and `ps -Ao pid,ppid,pcpu,etime,comm -r` at 04:48:09Z.
